simple.meaning: יַת (yath) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a sign of the object of a verb.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 3:12. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יַת (H3487) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יַת (yath) / H3487 is traced through Daniel 3:12 with source-language evidence and verse context.

structuredEvidence.definition: a sign of the object of a verb

firstOccurrence.englishText: There are certain Jews whom you have appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men, O king, have not respected you. They don’t serve your gods, and don’t worship the golden image which you have set up.”
